description:
Who lives here: median age and the shares under 18 and 65 or over ([B01002](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B01002), [B01001](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B01001)), the four mutually exclusive non-Hispanic race shares this catalog carries — White, Black or African American, American Indian and Alaska Native, Asian — plus Hispanic or Latino of any race and its complement, people of color ([B03002](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B03002)), and the share of adults 25 and over holding a bachelor's degree or higher ([B15003](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B15003)).

Curated indicators for all **441** congressional districts of the 119th Congress in the United States, Puerto Rico and the island areas, from the U.S. Census Bureau's [American Community Survey](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs.html) **2020–2024 5-year estimates** (`acsdt5y2024`, the table-based [Summary File](https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/summary_file/2024/table-based-SF/data/5YRData/)). The Census Bureau calls the ACS "the premier source of detailed information about the nation's people and housing". The Bureau also publishes 1-year estimates at this geography; the 5-year release is used throughout this catalog so every geography in it is the same vintage and directly comparable.

Every estimate ships with its margin of error — `<column>_moe`, at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes — and the headline statistics also carry a coefficient of variation (`<column>_cv` = `moe / 1.645 / estimate`) so small-area noise can be flagged rather than mapped as if certain. Derived percentages propagate error with the Census Bureau's own formulas from [ACS Accuracy of the Data](https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/tech_docs/accuracy/MultiyearACSAccuracyofData2024.pdf): sums add in quadrature, proportions use the subset formula with the ratio formula as fallback. ACS jam values for suppressed or unestimable cells are NULL here, never numbers, and medians are published as the Bureau publishes them — a median cannot be aggregated to a larger area. Each column's description names its ACS table, its exact universe, and the lines summed to make it.

Districts are equal-population by construction — 546,488 to 1,021,191 people across the 435 voting districts, 771,301 at the median of all 437 rows with data (measured) — so the distribution of every rate here is far tighter than at any other geography, and the map styles' class breaks are measured accordingly. These are the districts of the **119th Congress** ([the vintage this ACS release tabulates](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/geography-acs/geography-boundaries-by-year/2024.html)); district numbers are not stable across congresses, so do not join these GEOIDs to an earlier congress's districts of the same number. Nothing is suppressed beyond the four island-area delegate districts, which are NULL on every column (**0.91%** of rows).

Geometries are the Census Bureau's [2024 cartographic boundary files](https://www.census.gov/geographies/mapping-files/time-series/geo/cartographic-boundary.html) for congressional districts of the 119th Congress (GENZ2024, 1:500,000), reprojected to EPSG:4326 and joined on `GEOID`. Cartographic rather than TIGER/Line because TIGER extends census geographies into open water while the cartographic files clip to the shoreline, which is what a choropleth wants. The file is `cb_2024_us_cd119_500k` — `CDSESSN = '119'` on all 441 features — matching the congress this release tabulates.

The join is driven by geometry, so a geography with 2024 boundaries but no ACS tabulation keeps its row with NULL values instead of disappearing: 4 delegate districts (American Samoa, Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands, the U.S. Virgin Islands) in the island areas, which have cartographic boundaries but no ACS 5-year estimates because the Island Areas run a separate decennial-only program. In the other direction, three ACS district rows have no polygon and so no row here: `09ZZ`, `17ZZ` and `33ZZ`, the water-only pseudo-districts Connecticut, Illinois and New Hampshire contribute to the tabulation, each with population 0. Keeping these rows means a national map has no holes and a consumer can see the absence; dropping them would make "every US geography" quietly mean something narrower.

This is one themed chunk of six at this geography. The other themes are [Income & Poverty](../cd-income/collection.json), [Housing & Rent](../cd-housing/collection.json), [Commuting & Connectivity](../cd-connectivity/collection.json) and [Health, Disability & Income by Race](../cd-wellbeing/collection.json), split that way so a consumer who wants one theme reads one file. Chunks at the same geography hold the same rows and the same geometry, so they join 1:1 on `geoid`. A sixth collection, [All Indicators](../congressional-districts/collection.json), carries all 135 columns on the same rows in one wide table — at this many features width costs little, so take that one if a question crosses themes. A district nests in a state, so `substr(geoid, 1, 2)` reaches the state row; nothing finer joins by prefix, because district boundaries follow 2020 census blocks rather than counties or tracts. Every other geography in this catalog is organized the same way — [block groups](../../block-groups/catalog.json), [census tracts](../../tracts/catalog.json), [counties](../../counties/catalog.json), [states](../../states/catalog.json), [ZCTAs](../../zctas/catalog.json) and [places and CDPs](../../places/catalog.json) — and the [blocks](../../blocks/collection.json) collection carries 2020 Decennial counts, a different survey and vintage rather than a finer version of these numbers.

The PMTiles archive carries the same columns as the GeoParquet, minus the `*_moe` columns, and at every zoom the tiles are the real census geographies — there are few enough features here to draw them all at a national zoom, so this archive needs none of the coarser-geography coarse-zoom bands the catalog's finer collections carry. Built with [tylertoo](https://github.com/geoparquet-io/tylertoo). Statistics still come from the GeoParquet: margins of error are not in the tiles.

This is a mirror — [data.census.gov](https://data.census.gov/) is authoritative, and nothing here is an official Census Bureau product. The exact upstream files this collection was built from are published as `source` assets, linked at their original census.gov URLs, so the original is always one click away; the Bureau's own documentation is linked alongside them. Read the collection's [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) before querying: it carries the schema, the join keys, the NULL-rate story and tested queries against the published URLs.

source-table-shells.title: ACS 2020–2024 5-year table shells

Two jobs here: every line number the build reads is pinned against this file and a vintage that renumbers a line fails the build, and every universe quoted in the column descriptions is this file's own `Universe` field. Served by census.gov.

source-cartographic-boundaries.title: 2024 cartographic boundary file — congressional districts of the 119th Congress (1:500,000, national)
source-cartographic-boundaries.description: The geometry this collection joins onto, shoreline-clipped and generalized for mapping. Only the join key, the name parts and the land-area field are kept; reprojected from NAD83 to EPSG:4326 with ogr2ogr. `CDSESSN = '119'` on every feature, matching the congress this ACS release tabulates. Served by census.gov.

doc-geo-tallies.title: 2020 Census national geographic entity tallies
doc-geo-tallies.description: The published count of every geographic entity type, which this collection's row count is checked against: 33,791 ZCTAs (33,642 US + 132 Puerto Rico + 17 island areas), 19,734 incorporated places and 12,454 census designated places, 441 congressional districts (436 US including the DC delegate + 1 Puerto Rico + 4 island areas). Index page: https://www.census.gov/geographies/reference-files/time-series/geo/tallies.html.

doc-cd119.title: Congressional Districts of the 119th Congress — Census Bureau
doc-cd119.description: The Bureau's page for the district plans this collection maps. The vintage is confirmed by https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/geography-acs/geography-boundaries-by-year/2024.html, which lists "Congressional District, Delegate District DC, Resident Commissioner District PR" with a vintage of "119th Congress of the United States" for the 2024 ACS.

doc-acs-handbook.title: Understanding and Using American Community Survey Data — Census Bureau handbooks
doc-acs-handbook.description: The Bureau's own guidance on what ACS estimates can and cannot support: 1-year versus 5-year releases, margins of error, comparing across vintages, and small-area reliability. Read it before drawing a conclusion from a single block group.

doc-acs-accuracy.title: ACS Accuracy of the Data (2024, multiyear estimates)
doc-acs-accuracy.description: The source of every margin-of-error formula this build applies: quadrature for sums, the proportion formula and its ratio fallback for percentages, and the definition of the published 90% confidence level.

doc-acs-subject-definitions.title: ACS 2024 Subject Definitions
doc-acs-subject-definitions.description: The Census Bureau's definitions of the concepts behind these columns — household, householder, gross rent, poverty status determined, group quarters, means of transportation to work, disability. Where a column description here says what a universe is, this is the document it is saying it from.

doc-geo-glossary.title: Census Bureau geography program glossary
doc-geo-glossary.description: Definitions of the geographies and the identifiers used here — block, block group, tract, county equivalent, GEOID, and what nests inside what.

table:columns.name: geoid
table:columns.description: 4-character congressional district GEOID — state FIPS (2) + district (2), e.g. `0612` for California's 12th. `substr(geoid, 1, 2)` is the state FIPS code. At-large states use district `00` (AK, DE, ND, SD, VT, WY) and the non-voting delegate districts use `98` (`1198` District of Columbia, `7298` Puerto Rico, plus the four island areas). Districts of the **119th Congress**, which is the vintage the ACS 2020–2024 5-year release tabulates: matches `GEOID` in the `cb_2024_us_cd119_500k` cartographic boundary file (`CDSESSN = '119'` on every feature) and the ACS `5001900US` prefix, whose `19` is the congress number, is stripped. District numbers are not stable across congresses, so a `geoid` here does not join to a 118th-Congress district of the same number.

table:columns.name: name
table:columns.description: `NAMELSAD` from the cartographic boundary congressional district file plus the state name from the state file — "Congressional District 12, California", "Delegate District (at Large), District of Columbia".

table:columns.name: state
table:columns.description: Two-letter USPS state or territory code (`MO`, `PR`, `GU`). Carried on every collection from the `STATEFP → USPS` lookup embedded in `tools/specs.py` rather than read off the boundary files, because the 2024 cartographic boundary block-group file has no `STUSPS` column while the tract, county and state files do.

table:columns.name: population
table:columns.description: Total population. Universe: total population. The single line of [B01003](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B01003) (Total Population), published as an integer. Carried on every ACS collection so a rate can be weighted or sanity-checked without a second download. NULL on 0.91% of districts — the four island-area delegate districts (American Samoa, Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands, the U.S. Virgin Islands), which have 2024 boundaries but no ACS 5-year estimates. Every other column in this collection is NULL on the same four rows and nowhere else.

table:columns.name: population_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `population` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Component margins add in quadrature — `sqrt(Σ moe²)` — which is the Census Bureau's formula for the margin of a sum. NULL when every component is a jam value.

table:columns.name: aland_sqkm
table:columns.description: Land area in square kilometres, rounded to 3 decimals. `ALAND / 1e6` from the cartographic boundary file. Land only: water area is excluded, which is what makes it the right denominator for population density.

table:columns.name: pop_density
table:columns.description: People per square kilometre of land area, rounded to 1 decimal: `population / aland_sqkm`. NULL where `ALAND` is 0 or `population` is NULL.

table:columns.name: median_age
table:columns.description: Median age in years. Universe: total population. Line 1 of [B01002](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B01002) (Median Age by Sex); the male and female medians on lines 2 and 3 are not published here. Like every median, not aggregable.

table:columns.name: median_age_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `median_age` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Published as the Census Bureau publishes it for this line. A median's margin cannot be recomputed from a distribution, so it is passed through untouched.

table:columns.name: pct_under_18
table:columns.description: Percent of the population under 18 years old. Universe: total population. The under-18 lines of [B01001](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B01001) (Sex by Age) over line 1. The components are resolved from the table shells by label — "Under 5 years", "5 to 9 years", "10 to 14 years", "15 to 17 years", once per sex, 8 lines for this vintage — so a renumbered line fails the build instead of silently shifting.

table:columns.name: pct_under_18_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `pct_under_18` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Propagated with the Census Bureau's proportion formula, `sqrt(moe_num² − p²·moe_den²) / den`, falling back to the ratio formula (`+` instead of `−`) when the radicand goes negative because the numerator is not a true subset of the denominator. Multiplied by 100 to match the percentage, rounded to 2 decimals, and NULL rather than guessed when an input margin is NULL or the denominator is 0.

table:columns.name: pct_65_plus
table:columns.description: Percent of the population 65 years and over. Universe: total population. The 65-and-over lines of [B01001](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B01001) over line 1, resolved from the shells by label ("65 and 66 years" through "85 years and over", once per sex, 12 lines for this vintage).

table:columns.name: pct_65_plus_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `pct_65_plus` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Propagated with the Census Bureau's proportion formula, `sqrt(moe_num² − p²·moe_den²) / den`, falling back to the ratio formula (`+` instead of `−`) when the radicand goes negative because the numerator is not a true subset of the denominator. Multiplied by 100 to match the percentage, rounded to 2 decimals, and NULL rather than guessed when an input margin is NULL or the denominator is 0.

table:columns.name: pct_white_nh
table:columns.description: Percent of the population that is White alone and not Hispanic or Latino. Universe: total population. Line 3 of [B03002](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B03002) over line 1 — line 3 sits under line 2, "Not Hispanic or Latino", so this is the non-Hispanic branch.

table:columns.name: pct_white_nh_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `pct_white_nh` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Propagated with the Census Bureau's proportion formula, `sqrt(moe_num² − p²·moe_den²) / den`, falling back to the ratio formula (`+` instead of `−`) when the radicand goes negative because the numerator is not a true subset of the denominator. Multiplied by 100 to match the percentage, rounded to 2 decimals, and NULL rather than guessed when an input margin is NULL or the denominator is 0.

table:columns.name: pct_black
table:columns.description: Percent of the population that is Black or African American alone and not Hispanic or Latino. Universe: total population. Line 4 of [B03002](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B03002) over line 1 (the "Not Hispanic or Latino" branch, so this share and `pct_hispanic` do not overlap).

table:columns.name: pct_black_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `pct_black` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Propagated with the Census Bureau's proportion formula, `sqrt(moe_num² − p²·moe_den²) / den`, falling back to the ratio formula (`+` instead of `−`) when the radicand goes negative because the numerator is not a true subset of the denominator. Multiplied by 100 to match the percentage, rounded to 2 decimals, and NULL rather than guessed when an input margin is NULL or the denominator is 0.

table:columns.name: pct_native
table:columns.description: Percent of the population that is American Indian and Alaska Native alone and not Hispanic or Latino. Universe: total population. Line 5 of [B03002](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B03002) over line 1. Small everywhere outside Indian Country and reservations, and at block-group scale usually within its own margin of error.

table:columns.name: pct_native_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `pct_native` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Propagated with the Census Bureau's proportion formula, `sqrt(moe_num² − p²·moe_den²) / den`, falling back to the ratio formula (`+` instead of `−`) when the radicand goes negative because the numerator is not a true subset of the denominator. Multiplied by 100 to match the percentage, rounded to 2 decimals, and NULL rather than guessed when an input margin is NULL or the denominator is 0.

table:columns.name: pct_asian
table:columns.description: Percent of the population that is Asian alone and not Hispanic or Latino. Universe: total population. Line 6 of [B03002](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B03002) over line 1.

table:columns.name: pct_asian_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `pct_asian` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Propagated with the Census Bureau's proportion formula, `sqrt(moe_num² − p²·moe_den²) / den`, falling back to the ratio formula (`+` instead of `−`) when the radicand goes negative because the numerator is not a true subset of the denominator. Multiplied by 100 to match the percentage, rounded to 2 decimals, and NULL rather than guessed when an input margin is NULL or the denominator is 0.

table:columns.name: pct_hispanic
table:columns.description: Percent of the population that is Hispanic or Latino, of any race. Universe: total population. Line 12 of [B03002](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B03002) over line 1. Hispanic origin is asked separately from race, which is why this crosses every race category; here it is disjoint from the five race shares because those are all drawn from the non-Hispanic branch.

table:columns.name: pct_hispanic_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `pct_hispanic` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Propagated with the Census Bureau's proportion formula, `sqrt(moe_num² − p²·moe_den²) / den`, falling back to the ratio formula (`+` instead of `−`) when the radicand goes negative because the numerator is not a true subset of the denominator. Multiplied by 100 to match the percentage, rounded to 2 decimals, and NULL rather than guessed when an input margin is NULL or the denominator is 0.

table:columns.name: pct_people_of_color
table:columns.description: Percent of the population that is **not** White-alone non-Hispanic: `100 − pct_white_nh`. Universe: total population. Derived from [B03002](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B03002). A complement, so it carries `pct_white_nh`'s own margin of error unchanged — a share and its complement have the same sampling error.

table:columns.name: pct_people_of_color_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `pct_people_of_color` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. A complement carries the margin of error of the share it was taken from, unchanged — `100 − p` has the same sampling error as `p`.

table:columns.name: pct_bachelors_plus
table:columns.description: Percent of adults 25 and over whose highest attainment is a bachelor's degree or more. Universe: population 25 years and over. Lines 22–25 of [B15003](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B15003) (Bachelor's, Master's, Professional school, Doctorate) over line 1. Associate's degrees (line 21) are deliberately excluded.

table:columns.name: pct_bachelors_plus_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `pct_bachelors_plus` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Propagated with the Census Bureau's proportion formula, `sqrt(moe_num² − p²·moe_den²) / den`, falling back to the ratio formula (`+` instead of `−`) when the radicand goes negative because the numerator is not a true subset of the denominator. Multiplied by 100 to match the percentage, rounded to 2 decimals, and NULL rather than guessed when an input margin is NULL or the denominator is 0.

table:columns.name: geometry
table:columns.description: Boundary polygon (Polygon or MultiPolygon), WKB-encoded, in EPSG:4326 / OGC:CRS84 — the GeoParquet default CRS, written as an omitted `crs` key. From the Census Bureau's 2024 cartographic boundary congressional district file (GENZ2024, 1:500,000), which clips to the shoreline — TIGER/Line would extend the congressional district into open water. Generalized for mapping and point-in-polygon work, not for legal-boundary or precise-area work.

table:columns.name: bbox
table:columns.type: struct<xmin: double, ymin: double, xmax: double, ymax: double>
table:columns.description: GeoParquet 1.1 covering struct (`xmin`, `ymin`, `xmax`, `ymax`) for the row's geometry, with row-group statistics, so a spatial filter can skip most of the file over the network. Written by geoparquet-io, not by the Census Bureau.
